title: Each Insufficient in Its Own Way: Calibrating Language Models Across Varying Evidence States
abstract: arXiv:2610.33237v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How can a language model know whether it has enough evidence to answer? Language models tend to answer even when the evidence they have is insufficient. Deciding whether to answer or gather more evidence requires a calibrated estimate of how likely an answer is to be correct with the available evidence. However, most calibration work treats the input as fixed, without asking how this estimate should change with the evidence. We introduce \emph{evidence-state calibration}, which requires a model's confidence before answering to match its probability of answering correctly and to change accordingly whenever the evidence changes this probability. We propose \ours{} (\textbf{Suffi}ciency \textbf{C}onfidence \textbf{E}stimation), which fine-tunes the confidence already present in a model's next-token distribution to match how often the model answers correctly from each evidence state. Across clinical diagnosis and multi-hop question answering

translated_title: 各有各的不足：跨不同证据状态校准语言模型
translated_abstract: 语言模型如何知道自己是否拥有足够的证据来回答问题？即使现有证据不充分，语言模型也倾向于直接作答。决定是回答还是继续收集更多证据，需要对“在现有证据下答案正确的可能性”进行校准估计。然而，大多数校准工作都将输入视为固定的，而没有探究这一估计应如何随证据的变化而变化。我们提出了“证据状态校准”（evidence-state calibration），它要求模型在回答前的置信度与其正确回答的概率相匹配，并且每当证据改变这一概率时，置信度也应相应变化。我们提出了SuffiCE（充分性置信度估计，Sufficiency Confidence Estimation），该方法对模型下一词元分布中已存在的置信度进行微调，使其匹配模型在每种证据状态下回答正确的频率。在临床诊断和多跳问答任务上……
tldr: 提出证据状态校准的新范式与SuffiCE方法，通过微调模型下一词元分布中已有的置信度，使模型置信度随证据状态的变化而与其实际回答正确的概率保持一致。
en_tdlr: Proposes evidence-state calibration and SuffiCE, a method that fine-tunes the confidence already present in a model's next-token distribution so that confidence matches and tracks its probability of answering correctly across varying evidence states.
